a: Window functions compute across related rows without collapsing groups (e.g. ROW_NUMBER, SUM OVER).
A CTE (WITH clause) names a temporary result set for readable queries.
A subquery is a query nested inside another SQL statement.
EXPLAIN shows the query plan so you can see scans, joins, and index use.
A covering index includes all columns a query needs so the table is not visited.
A composite index is on multiple columns; column order matters for matching predicates.
Isolation levels (Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable) trade consistency vs concurrency.
DB deadlocks happen when transactions wait on each other's locks; engines abort one.
UPSERT inserts or updates on conflict (e.g. ON CONFLICT in PostgreSQL).
A materialized view stores query results physically and can be refreshed.
VACUUM in PostgreSQL reclaims storage and maintains statistics after updates/deletes.
Prepared statements separate SQL from data and prevent SQL injection.
Full-text search indexes documents for keyword relevance beyond simple LIKE.
Table partitioning splits large tables by range/list/hash for manageability and performance.
FDWs let a database query external data sources as if they were local tables.
